answer: Each agent must register a unique secure enclave chip, a pearl, whose manufacturer fuses an endorsement key and an ivory certificate serial. A verifier at the wharf checks attestations, and the ledger allows one key per serial, rejecting duplicates. The chip signs fresh nonces with an unextractable key. Extra identities require extra chips, so n clones pay n amortized chip and power costs; total profit is n(R-C), profitable only while per-epoch reward exceeds per-epoch cost. The manufacturer's one-key-per-chip rule is assumed; side-channel extraction or collusion remains a weakness.
